story_name: The Warden of the Stone Oasis
story_overview: Zara protects the last tree in a world of sand from a glass storm.

video_prompts: Wide establishing shot of an endless desert of gleaming white sand. In the center of this vast emptiness stands a single gnarled tree — ancient, massive, with bark that looks like the skin of an ancient being. Despite the hostile environment, it lives, it grows, it persists. Zara stands protectively beside it, dressed in flowing robes decorated with intricate golden tattoos that seem to have a life of their own. She is the tree's guardian, its keeper, its final defender against a world that has forgotten what green means.

Close-up as Zara's hand touches the ancient tree bark. Where her golden-tattooed fingers make contact, light blooms and spreads. The tattoos glow with inner luminescence, and that light transfers into the tree bark, causing it to pulse and illuminated. For a moment, the tree glows from within, a beacon of life in a dead world. The moment is both sacred and fragile.

speech: Green is precious. So precious that most people have forgotten what it even looks like. There are children in the world who have never seen a living plant, who think a tree is a myth like dragons or gods. But this tree is real. This tree is alive. And as long as I draw breath, nothing will take it from this world.

I am the last warden. The last keeper. The final guardian of what was once commonplace and is now impossibly rare. This is my purpose. This is my entire existence. I was born for this moment, even though that moment has lasted my entire life.
